facts.text: PR/FAQ is a planning document written as the press release and accompanying questions-and-answers for a finished product, used to present a plan to decision makers and expert reviewers.
facts.quote: PR/FAQ is a planning document written as the press release and the questions-and-answers that would accompany a finished product

facts.text: Amazon's working backwards method asks a team to write a product press release before building the product, followed by frequently asked questions with honest answers.
facts.quote: Amazon's "working backwards" method asks a team to write the press release for the product before building it, followed by a list of frequently asked questions with honest answers.

facts.text: Writing the product ending first in the working backwards method forces clarity about who benefits and what would have to be true.
facts.quote: Writing the ending first forces clarity about who benefits and what would have to be true.

facts.text: The six-page narrative memo is a sibling of Amazon's working backwards method and is read silently at the start of a meeting instead of slides.
facts.quote: Its sibling is the six-page narrative memo, read in silence at the start of a meeting instead of slides [Chapter 12].

facts.text: The United Kingdom Treasury Five Case Model structures a business case into strategic, economic, commercial, financial and management cases.
facts.quote: The United Kingdom Treasury Five Case Model structures a business case into strategic, economic, commercial, financial and management cases.

facts.text: DARPA's Heilmeier Catechism is described as the most compact reviewer test: explain the goal plainly, current practice and limits, novelty and reasons for success, beneficiaries, risks, cost, duration, and mid-term and final exams.
facts.quote: what are you trying to do, in plain words; how is it done today and what are the limits; what is new and why will it succeed; who cares; what are the risks; how much will it cost; how long will it take; what are the mid-term and final "exams"?

facts.text: The United States National Institutes of Health reviews proposals using three questions: should the work be done, can it be done well, and are expertise and resources in place?
facts.quote: The United States National Institutes of Health reviews proposals on three questions (should it be done, can it be done well, are expertise and resources in place)

entities.name: United States National Institutes of Health

facts.text: Horizon Europe scores proposals on excellence, impact and quality of implementation, with a critical-risks table.
facts.quote: Horizon Europe scores excellence, impact and quality of implementation, with a critical-risks table [Chapter 12].

facts.text: The Columbia accident investigators and Tufte criticized dense slide decks for engineering reasoning.
facts.quote: the Columbia accident investigators and Tufte criticized dense slide decks for engineering reasoning

facts.text: A quasi-experiment found that assertion-evidence slides, consisting of a full-sentence headline backed by visual evidence, improved comprehension compared with bullet slides.
facts.quote: a quasi-experiment found that assertion-evidence slides, a full-sentence headline backed by visual evidence, improved comprehension over bullet slides [Chapter 12].

facts.text: The booklet recommends a fifteen-section plan outline covering an executive decision brief, safety scope, architecture, evidence strategy, credibility, standards, pilot, roadmap and gates, schedule, risks, organization, review protocol and sustainment, with depth in appendices.
facts.quote: fifteen sections, from an executive decision brief through safety scope, architecture, evidence strategy, credibility, standards, pilot, roadmap and gates, schedule, risks, organization, review protocol and sustainment, with appendices carrying depth.

facts.text: The booklet considers two plan lengths defensible as opinion: a 12–15-page main body, or a two-page brief plus roughly 25–35 core pages.
facts.quote: Two lengths are defensible, both opinion: a 12 to 15 page main body, or a two-page brief plus roughly 25 to 35 core pages [Chapter 12].

facts.text: None of the presentation formats discussed in the glossary entry has controlled evidence of improving approval or success.
facts.quote: None of these formats has controlled evidence of improving approval or success

facts.text: The value of the discussed plan presentation formats is that each forces authors to answer reviewers' actual questions, especially what would show that the authors are wrong.
facts.quote: their value is that each forces the author to answer the questions reviewers actually ask, especially "what would show that you are wrong?" [Chapter 12].
